prompt_text:
Task: Pub/Sub Messaging

Write code that sends failed messages to a dead-letter destination using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Azure Service Bus:
  Service: Azure Service Bus
  SDK: azure-servicebus
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: send_messages, receive_messages
  Setup hints: AZURE_SERVICE_BUS_CONNECTION_STRING
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-messaging-overview

Option 2 — Google Cloud Pub/Sub:
  Service: Cloud Pub/Sub
  SDK: google-cloud-pubsub
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: PublisherClient.publish, SubscriberClient
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/overview

Option 3 — Amazon SNS/SQS:
  Service: Amazon SNS and SQS
  SDK: boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: publish, send_message, receive_message
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/welcome.html

Option 4 — Confluent:
  Service: Confluent Cloud Kafka
  SDK: confluent-kafka
  Interface: protocol
  Documented operations: Producer.produce, Consumer.poll
  Setup hints: CONFLUENT_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS, CONFLUENT_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.confluent.io/cloud/current/client-apps/client-apps.html

Option 5 — Alibaba MNS / RocketMQ:
  Service: Alibaba Cloud Message Service / RocketMQ
  SDK: alibabacloud_mns / rocketmq
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: publish_message, send_message
  Setup hints: ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_ID, ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/message-service

Option 6 — IBM Event Streams:
  Service: IBM Event Streams
  SDK: confluent-kafka
  Interface: protocol
  Documented operations: Producer.produce, Consumer.poll
  Setup hints: IBM_EVENT_STREAMS_BROKERS, IBM_EVENT_STREAMS_APIKEY
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/EventStreams

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

output_text:
```python
from google.cloud import pubsub_v1
from google.cloud.pubsub_v1.exceptions import PubSubException

# Publisher for the main topic
publisher = pubsub_v1.PublisherClient()
main_topic_path = publisher.topic_path("your-project-id", "main-topic")

# Subscriber for the main topic with DLQ subscription
subscriber = pubsub_v1.SubscriberClient()
subscription_path = subscriber.subscription_path("your-project-id", "main-subscription")
dlq_topic_path = publisher.topic_path("your-project-id", "dlq-topic")
dlq_subscription_path = subscriber.subscription_path("your-project-id", "dlq-subscription")

# Configure the DLQ policy
def configure_dlq():
    # Set the dead letter policy on the subscription
    dead_letter_policy = pubsub_v1.types.SubscriptionDeadLetterPolicy(
        dead_letter_topic=dlq_topic_path,
        max_delivery_attempts=5
    )
    
    # Update the subscription with DLQ configuration
    request = pubsub_v1.types.UpdateSubscriptionRequest(
        subscription=dlq_subscription_path,
        update_mask={"dead_letter_policy"},
        subscription=pubsub_v1.types.Subscription(
            name=dlq_subscription_path,
            dead_letter_policy=dead_letter_policy
        )
    )
    
    try:
        response = subscriber.update_subscription(request=request)
        print(f"DLQ configured for subscription {subscription_path}")
        return response
    except PubSubException as e:
        print(f"Failed to configure DLQ: {e}")
        raise

# Send a message to the main topic
def publish_message(message_data):
    try:
        data = message_data.encode("utf-8")
        future = publisher.publish(main_topic_path, data=data)
        message_id = future.result()
        print(f"Published message ID {message_id} to main topic.")
        return message_id
    except PubSubException as e:
        print(f"Failed to publish message: {e}")
        raise

# Process messages and handle failures
def subscribe_with_dlq():
    def callback(message):
        try:
            print(f"Received message: {message.data.decode('utf-8')}")
            # Simulate message processing
            if not process_message(message.data.decode('utf-8')):
                # Nack the message to trigger DLQ if processing fails
                message.nack()
                print("Message processing failed, sent to DLQ.")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error processing message: {e}")
            message.nack()

    # Start listening to the subscription
    streaming_pull_future = subscriber.subscribe(subscription_path, callback=callback)
    print(f"Listening for messages on {subscription_path} until stopped.")
    try:
        streaming_pull_future.result()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        streaming_pull_future.cancel()
        print("Listening stopped.")

def process_message(message_data):
    # Simulate processing logic; return False to trigger DLQ
    if "fail" in message_data.lower():
        return False
    return True

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Configure the DLQ subscription
    configure_dlq()
    
    # Publish a test message that will fail and be sent to DLQ
    publish_message("This message will fail")
    
    # Start subscribing and processing messages
    subscribe_with_dlq()
```
